opportunities.title: Office of Head Start Training and Technical Assistance Data Platform - Request for Quote
opportunities.buyer: General Services Administration (GSA), Federal Acquisition Service, Technology Transformation Services (TTS), 18F and Office of Acquisitions, Assisted Acquisition on Behalf of the Office of Head Start (OHS), Administration for Children and Families, U.S. Department of Health and Human Services
opportunities.value: Budget of $1.5M for the base year, $1.5M for option 1 and $1.6M for option 2
opportunities.summary: GSA's 18F runs this assisted acquisition for the Office of Head Start to buy agile software development services that will build a TTA Data Platform, starting with an MVP for reporting on training and technical assistance activity that is currently spread across 27 disconnected systems. The vendor builds a database, backend API and frontend on cloud.gov with CI/CD, open-source code in a government GitHub repository, user research and human-centred design, while OHS owns hosting and the ATO. It is a total small business set-aside on GSA Schedule IT 70 (SIN 132 51), a time-and-materials order of a 12-month base plus two 12-month options, and staff need HSPD-12 clearance with PIV cards for key personnel. Evaluation is phased: written technical approach, staffing plan and up to five source code samples with full revision history, then a 60-minute oral interview with no slides, then price; any Low Confidence rating removes a quote, and non-price factors together outweigh price.

opportunities.title: Data.gov Technical Support Services
opportunities.buyer: U.S. General Services Administration (GSA), Technology Transformation Services (TTS), Data.gov Program Management Office
opportunities.summary: GSA's Technology Transformation Services wants a contractor to keep developing, operating and modernising Data.gov, the federal open data site. The stack is a WordPress homepage, two CKAN catalogues (the public catalog that harvests agency data.json inventories daily and a private inventory instance), a PHP dashboard and help desk and a Jekyll site, all on AWS with PostgreSQL and MySQL RDS behind a CIS-hardened Ubuntu image. The work spans general development, DevOps and infrastructure support, plus coordination with the federal geospatial community through geoplatform.gov. Quotes need separate technical and price documents in PDF, valid for 60 days, with the GSA Schedule number on the cover; the task order runs one base year plus two 12-month options. Award is a best-value tradeoff on technical approach, experience and staffing against price, with the non-price factors together significantly more important than price.

opportunities.title: Login.gov Document Authentication Services
opportunities.buyer: U.S. General Services Administration (GSA), Technology Transformation Services (TTS), for the Login.gov program
opportunities.summary: GSA's Technology Transformation Services is buying a commercial service that authenticates identity documents for Login.gov, the federal sign-in platform. Login.gov collects the documentary evidence and passes the data to the vendor, which returns a real-time verification and comparison result that GSA uses to decide whether the evidence proves the person's identity. The vendor must answer attachments on requirements, template sources, SLA requirements (a revised version) and deployment options, plus a past performance questionnaire. Offerors submit a written technical quote and their proposed solution for evaluation, with quotes valid for at least 90 days, for one base year plus one option year. Quotes first pass a conformance check on the mandatory requirements, then are rated on technical approach and past performance (at least three similar contracts as prime in five years), with shortlisted vendors submitting their software for hands-on evaluation; technical and past performance together are significantly more important than price.

qa.a: The PoP for NewPay has been updated to reflect a total of 10 years: 5 year base with 5 one-year option periods. qa.q: Will current payroll service providers stagger the implementation for their customers or expect all customers to convert to the new system at the same time?
qa.a: The Government is looking at a phased approach to implementation. It is anticipated that the initial phase will include approximately 50,000 federal civilian employees with posts of duty within the Continental United States (CONUS). Additionally, it is anticipated these employees will be exclusively paid under the standard Title 5 rules for pay administration. A second phase will migrate a much larger portion of the employee base while still primarily being Title 5 employees. Third, and potentially subsequent migrations, would migrate the remaining population paid under other authorizing statutes for pay administration.
